ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver.

rejected_claims.reason: Partly rejected: the rider's claim that the 2 min 55 s post-tap window is the only measure fails as an inference of law — F6 does show 175 s continuously inside the radius after the 13:02:45 tap, but NS-1 (iii) is failed on that fact only in combination with the settled trace, and the claim's framing that the earlier 4 min 30 s presence [F2] is irrelevant goes further than NS-1 requires; the fee nonetheless fails (NS-2).

Rejected in part: the rider's reading that a chat message of 13:05 ('Waited more than 3 min, cancelling', F10) 'confirms' the driver genuinely waited over three minutes is the opposite of what the message shows in context — it is the driver's own contemporaneous assertion, and the post-tap system window [F6] contradicts it; the fee is refunded on NS-2, not because the message validates the driver's account (NS-1).

Rejected as immaterial: traffic band 3 on Tampines Street 82 [F13], no incidents [F14] and fair weather [F15] concern RD-4 excuses for rerouting, and no reroute is alleged and no route-related amount is charged in this no-show dispute (RD-4).

Rejected as a basis for the outcome: the rider's clean profile, 4.0 years, 4.9 rating, 0 disputes [F16], is a profile fact and cannot alone decide the case (procedure); the refund rests on the NS-1 (iii) failure shown by F6/F3, not on the rider's history (NS-2 does not condition on profile).

Accepted in outcome but noted: no account-level action is warranted on this file since the trace shows no fake tap [F6][F1] and the driver's 90-day record has 0 upheld disputes [F17]; the RD-6 flag condition (`route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1`) is not met, so the claim that no flag is warranted is correct (RD-6).

Rejected: the driver's claim that NS-1 (iii) is satisfied 'by either measure' misreads the rule — the 3 min 15 s stationary window [F3] and 4 min 30 s cumulative presence [F2] mostly precede the 13:02:45 arrival indication [F6], and only 2 min 55 s of qualifying wait follows the tap, short of ≥ 3:01 (NS-1).

Rejected: the 4 min 30 s from the platform-recorded arrival at 13:01:10 to the cancellation [F5][F4] does not satisfy NS-1 (iii) — the qualifying wait runs from the arrival indication at 13:02:45 [F6], and the cancellation came 2 min 55 s later (NS-1).
Rejected: the $6.61 fee does not stand under NS-1, so the requested no_action fails and the $4.50 driver share is not earned; NS-2 requires the full return of $6.61 (F7) [NS-1][NS-2].

Rejected: the claim that the 4 min 30 s arrival-to-cancellation gap [F5][F4] proves the rider failed to show is not supported — the gap measures only the driver's side, riders are not tracked, and the complaint's emergence time is a statement; the gap cannot cure the NS-1 (iii) shortfall measured from the tap [F6] (NS-4 does not apply; NS-1 governs).

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
